name: יִתְרוֹ
summary: The priest of Midian, Moses' father-in-law, whose flock Moses kept when Yahweh appeared to him at Horeb (Exo 3:1). He let Moses go back to Egypt (Exo 4:18), brought Zipporah and her sons to him in the wilderness, rejoiced at all the good Yahweh had done for Israel and blessed Yahweh, “now I know that Yahweh is greater than all the gods”, offered sacrifice, and counselled Moses to appoint judges (Exo 18:1–27). Once he is called יֶתֶר (Exo 4:18), and Exo 2:18 calls Zipporah's father Reuel. The name is יֶתֶר with the ending וֹ, read as “his abundance” or “his excellence”; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “Moses was keeping the flock of יִתְרוֹ his father-in-law, the priest of Midian.”
“Moses returned to יֶתֶר his father-in-law … and יִתְרוֹ said, Go in peace”: the two spellings in one verse.
“יִתְרוֹ the priest of Midian heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel.”
He rejoiced and said, “Blessed be Yahweh … now I know that Yahweh is greater than all the gods.”
He took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God, and ate bread with Aaron and the elders.
The noun יֶתֶר, “pre-eminence”, from which the name is formed.

note: Takes j.ef.ah (9 tokens, all Exodus 3–18). TIPNR's Jethro@Exo.2.18 also covers Reuel (names/reuel.json) and the יֶתֶר of Exo 4:18 (names/jether.json). The final וֹ is read as the suffix “his”; it may instead be a name ending, as in other names in -ō, and the meaning is a reading of the form only.
